annotation.title_clean: White Paper des Österreichischen Rats für Robotik und Künstliche Intelligenz
annotation.title_en: White Paper of the Austrian Council on Robotics and Artificial Intelligence
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Österreichischer Rat für Robotik und Künstliche Intelligenz (BMVIT advisory council)
annotation.venue: Austrian Council on Robotics and AI (acrai.at)
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: First white paper of the Austrian Council on Robotics and AI, advising the transport/innovation ministry. It sets out three cornerstones (smart governance, innovation, regulation) and four action fields: technology and economy, labour and skills, society and law, and public awareness. It recommends an incremental strategy process, sandboxes, certification and audit tools, and adapting liability rules.
key_provisions_or_claims: Recommends an incremental 'strategizing' process with feedback loops and technology monitoring, coordinated with EU activities.
Calls for targeted public investment, and for qualification and requalification of workers.
Proposes sandboxes and testbeds for high-risk, sensitive application areas.
Machines cannot bear moral responsibility; humans remain responsible. Liability rules, the Machinery Directive and criminal due-care standards should be adapted.
Recommends certification, auditing and compliance tools at EU level; AI systems should be explainable; robot legal personhood is not a priority but to be monitored.
